# Ceryx Provider

The Ceryx provider manages routes in a [Ceryx](https://github.com/withlogicco/ceryx) reverse proxy through its API. It reaches the API either at a URL (`endpoint`) or, when the API is only reachable inside its container, by running curl next to a container picked by a selector (`docker`).

## Example Usage

```terraform
terraform {
  required_providers {
    ceryx = {
      source = "withlogicco/ceryx"
    }
  }
}

# Ceryx runs as a Docker Swarm service on a remote host. Its API is not
# published, so the provider runs curl in a sidecar container that shares
# the Ceryx container's network namespace.
provider "ceryx" {
  docker {
    host = "ssh://root@proxy-01.example.com"

    container {
      labels = {
        "com.docker.swarm.service.name" = "ingress_ceryx"
      }
    }
  }
}

# A Compose project on the local Docker daemon, selected by labels. Its
# Ceryx image includes curl, so the provider runs curl there with docker exec.
provider "ceryx" {
  alias = "local"

  docker {
    container {
      labels = {
        "com.docker.compose.project" = "edge"
        "com.docker.compose.service" = "ceryx"
      }
    }

    connector {
      type = "exec"
    }
  }
}

# The API is reachable directly, for example from a container on the same
# Docker network or through an SSH tunnel.
provider "ceryx" {
  alias    = "direct"
  endpoint = "http://ceryx:8080"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `docker` (Block, Optional) Reach the API inside a Ceryx container on a Docker host. Each API request is one curl call, run in the network namespace of the container `container` selects, so the API needs no published port. `connector` chooses where curl runs. Conflicts with `endpoint`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--docker))
- `endpoint` (String) Ceryx API URL reachable from where Terraform runs, for example `http://ceryx:8080`. Defaults to `CERYX_ENDPOINT`. Conflicts with `docker`.

<a id="nestedblock--docker"></a>
### Nested Schema for `docker`

Optional:

- `api_url` (String) Ceryx API URL as seen from inside the container. Defaults to `http://127.0.0.1:8080`, where Ceryx serves its API. Older deployments with a separate `ceryx-api` container listen on `http://127.0.0.1:5555`.
- `connector` (Block, Optional) Where curl runs. Defaults to `sidecar`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--docker--connector))
- `container` (Block, Optional) Selects the Ceryx container among the running containers on the Docker host. Set at least one criterion; every criterion set must match, and exactly one container may match. The provider resolves the selector on every request, so it follows the container across restarts and redeploys. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--docker--container))
- `host` (String) Docker daemon address: `unix:///var/run/docker.sock`, `tcp://host:2376` or `ssh://user@host`. Defaults to `DOCKER_HOST`, then the local daemon. `tcp` hosts use `DOCKER_TLS_VERIFY` and `DOCKER_CERT_PATH`. `ssh` hosts run `docker system dial-stdio` through the local `ssh` command, so they use your SSH config and agent.

<a id="nestedblock--docker--connector"></a>
### Nested Schema for `docker.connector`

Optional:

- `image` (String) Image the `sidecar` connector runs, with `curl` on its `PATH`. Defaults to `curlimages/curl:8.10.1`. The Docker host pulls it on first use if it does not have it. Only valid with `type = "sidecar"`.
- `type` (String) `sidecar` runs curl in a throwaway container that joins the selected container's network namespace, like `docker run --rm --network container:<id> --entrypoint curl <image> ...`; it works whatever the Ceryx image contains. `exec` runs `docker exec <id> curl ...` in the selected container, which must include curl. Defaults to `sidecar`.


<a id="nestedblock--docker--container"></a>
### Nested Schema for `docker.container`

Optional:

- `id` (String) Container ID, or a unique prefix of one.
- `labels` (Map of String) Labels the container must carry, like `docker ps --filter label=...`. An empty value matches any value of that label. Select a Swarm service's tasks with `{ "com.docker.swarm.service.name" = "ingress_ceryx" }`, or a Compose service with `{ "com.docker.compose.service" = "ceryx" }`.
- `name` (String) Exact container name.
